author: Louis Dionne

evidence.note: R0 shows the author's original ask: a type-aware operator new/delete resolved via ADL with a std::type_identity tag, introduced between class-scope and global lookup. The revision history documents what he later conceded (ADL, argument order, mandatory implicit parameters, qualifier stripping) while keeping the core recommendation.
evidence.title: P2719R0: Type-aware allocation and deallocation functions
evidence.what_changed: R0 proposed ADL-based lookup for free-function type-aware operator new/delete, placed the std::type_identity tag after the size/pointer argument, restricted the feature to free functions, and did not yet add wording. By R1 the author dropped ADL based on implementation experience, moved std::type_identity to the first parameter as a tag, and allowed the parameter for in-class T::operator new for consistency; later revisions adopted EWG guidance (strip qualifiers, make all currently implicit parameters mandatory, make cross-scope selection ill-formed) and added wording.

evidence.note: R5 documents the author mid-stream position after the Hagenberg EWG review: the proposal had become a compiler-only overload-resolution change in global or class scope (no ADL), with std::type_identity first, mandatory size/alignment parameters, and qualifier stripping per EWG direction.
evidence.title: P2719R5: Type-aware allocation and deallocation functions
evidence.what_changed: Relative to R5, R7's biggest change was moving the overload-resolution parts of [expr.new] and [expr.delete] into new subclauses [over.match.new] and [over.match.delete] to address CWG feedback, rebasing on papers voted into the C++26 draft at Brno, and clarifying accessibility checks for deallocation functions. R5 itself already reflected post-Hagenberg EWG guidance: strip qualifiers in the type-identity type, make all currently implicit parameters mandatory, and make cross-scope type-aware new/new[] and delete/delete[] selection ill-formed.

evidence.note: In the same tracking thread, Louis Dionne (ldionne) personally argued for proceeding: he clarified that P2719R2, forwarded to CWG at Wrocław, was exactly the version discussed there, and that P2719R3 added only three 'small-ish design questions' he wanted EWG to consider in Hagenberg, framing the remaining changes as wording improvements. This shows him defending and shepherding the proposal through committee review.
evidence.title: Louis Dionne's comments on cplusplus/papers issue #1898

position: Louis Dionne is a lead author of P2719 and has consistently championed its core recommendation: passing the concrete type to operator new and operator delete via an implicit std::type_identity<T> tag argument, enabling type-specific and family-of-types allocators without intrusive class-scoped operators or whole-process overrides. The recorded revisions show he actively refined rather than abandoned the design — in R0 he proposed ADL-based free-function lookup with the tag after the size argument, then conceded ADL, moved std::type_identity to the first parameter for conflict safety, and adopted EWG guidance to strip qualifiers and make the otherwise-implicit size/alignment parameters mandatory for type-aware operators. On the record he explicitly rejected simpler alternatives such as a raw template argument or a T* tag, and refused type-aware destroying delete as a user hazard. In committee tracking, Dionne personally argued that P2719R3 added only three small design questions for EWG and that the rest were wording improvements, demonstrating that he was shepherding the proposal forward rather than conceding its core. Committee polls during this time showed repeated support for the direction he advocated.
recommendation: The paper proposes extending new-expressions and delete-expressions to pass the concrete type being allocated or deallocated to operator new and operator delete via an implicit std::type_identity<T> tag argument, enabling type-specific and family-of-types allocators without intrusive class-scoped operators or whole-process global overrides.
title: Type-aware allocation and deallocation functions
